connectSheet.getTheConnectionStringsAndEnvironment: Get the connection strings and environment variables for {{name}}.
connectSheet.replaceYourPasswordWithTheDatabase: Replace [YOUR-PASSWORD] with the database password. Your tools also need : add sslrootcert= and where you saved it.
connectSheet.installTheClientThenCreateIt: Install the client, then create it with your project URL and public key.
connectSheet.forYourAppSEnvironmentFile: For your app's environment file, such as .env.local in Next.js. The key is safe in a browser when Row Level Security is on.
connectSheet.thisProjectUsesSupermixerSOwn: This project uses Supermixer’s own certificate, which computers don’t trust until you tell them to. Download and add it to your computer’s trusted certificates. For Node.js, set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS to where you saved it.
connectSheet.psqlIsPostgresSOwnCommand: psql is Postgres's own command-line tool. To use it, you need a database login of your own.
connectSheet.thisProjectIsPausedStartIt: This project is paused. Start it first, under <link/>.
connectSheet.makeYourLoginInCreateA: Make your login. In , create a role. Give it a name and a password, and turn on Can log in. If you can't, ask whoever looks after this project to make one for you.
connectSheet.typeItHereAndTheCommands: Type it here and the commands below will use it.
connectSheet.letItReadYourTablesA: Let it read your tables. A new login can't see anything yet. Run this in the :
connectSheet.getTheCertificateYourConnectionIs: Get the certificate. Your connection is encrypted with Supermixer's own certificate. Download and save it as supermixer-ca.pem in the folder you'll run psql from.
connectSheet.connectRunThisInATerminal: Connect. Run this in a terminal. psql asks for your password, so it doesn't end up in your terminal's history.
connectSheet.ifPsqlSaysSslrootcertSystemIsn: If psql says sslrootcert=system isn't valid, it's older than version 16. Update it, or swap system for your computer's list of trusted certificates: /etc/ssl/cert.pem on a Mac, /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt on Ubuntu or Debian.
connectSheet.theAfterYourLoginSName: The {{suffix}} after your login's name tells the server which project you want, so leave it on.
connectSheet.checkItWorkedTypeSelectCurrent: Check it worked. Type select current_user; and you should see your login's name.
connectSheet.justChangedYourPasswordAndIt: Just changed your password and it isn't working? Give it a minute or two.

apiKeyList.publishableDescription: Safe to use in a browser if Row Level Security is enabled on your tables.
apiKeyList.secretDescription: Bypasses Row Level Security. Only use on a server; never expose it.
apiKeyList.anonDescription: Legacy public key. Safe in a browser if Row Level Security is enabled.
apiKeyList.serviceRoleDescription: Legacy secret key. Bypasses Row Level Security; never expose it.
apiKeyList.jwtSecretDescription: Signs the legacy JWT-based API keys and user sessions.

connectionForm.theStackSApiGatewaySupabase: The stack's API gateway: SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL in the Supabase stack's .env (port 8000 by default).
connectionForm.supabaseStacksUseLegacyJwtKeys: Supabase stacks use legacy JWT keys, the newer publishable and secret keys, or both. Secret keys are encrypted at rest.
connectionForm.selfHostedStacksPublishPostgresThrough: Self-hosted stacks publish Postgres through Supavisor on POSTGRES_PORT; the user is {{user}}, both from the Supabase stack's .env.
connectionForm.pasteTheSelfHostedSupabaseStack: Paste the self-hosted Supabase stack's .env: the file next to its docker-compose.yml (supabase/docker/.env in a Supabase checkout). This is not Supermixer's own .env.toml. It is read in your browser; nothing is saved until you create the project.
connectionForm.thisStackUsesSupabaseSExample: This stack uses Supabase's example secrets
connectionForm.exampleSecrets_one: The {{names}} is the public example from Supabase's self-hosting files, so anyone can use it: with the example JWT secret, anyone can sign a service_role token. Generate new secrets and restart the stack before you use it. Change the other example values in its .env too (DASHBOARD_PASSWORD, SECRET_KEY_BASE, VAULT_ENC_KEY, PG_META_CRYPTO_KEY, the Logflare tokens): Supermixer can't check those.
connectionForm.exampleSecrets_other: The {{names}} are the public example from Supabase's self-hosting files, so anyone can use them: with the example JWT secret, anyone can sign a service_role token. Generate new secrets and restart the stack before you use it. Change the other example values in its .env too (DASHBOARD_PASSWORD, SECRET_KEY_BASE, VAULT_ENC_KEY, PG_META_CRYPTO_KEY, the Logflare tokens): Supermixer can't check those.

createStack.supermixerStartsANewSelfHosted: Supermixer starts a new self-hosted Supabase stack on this server's Docker, with its own database, keys and ports.
createStack.everySecretIsGeneratedForThis: Every secret is generated for this stack: database password, JWT secret, API keys and encryption keys.
createStack.itGetsItsOwnPortsFor: It gets its own ports for the API and Postgres from the ranges this server is configured with.
createStack.itRunsSupabaseSOfficialDocker: It runs Supabase's official Docker setup at {{slice}}, with log analytics. The first stack can take several minutes while images download.

logDrains.batchesOfJsonLogEventsPosted: Batches of JSON log events, POSTed to your URL.
logDrains.pushedToLokiLabelledWithThe: Pushed to Loki, labelled with the project and service.
logDrains.sentToDatadogLogsWithYour: Sent to Datadog Logs with your API key.
logDrains.thereAreNoLogsToSend: There are no logs to send: Supermixer doesn't run Logflare and Vector for this project. Destinations can be removed, but not added or changed.
logDrains.logsFromTheApiGatewayAuth: Logs from the API gateway, Auth, the Data API, Realtime, Storage, Edge Functions and Postgres also go to these destinations. Each event carries supabase_service and supabase_project.
logDrains.name: Name
logDrains.logsLeaveFromTheStackS: Logs leave from the stack’s Vector container: to reach a service on the Supermixer server itself, use host.docker.internal rather than localhost. Saving checks the configuration with Vector, then restarts it.
logDrains.logsStopGoingToThisDestination: Logs stop going to this destination.
logDrains.lokiUrlHint: Its base URL, such as http://loki:3100

readOnlyAccess.howQueriesRunForMembersWith: How queries run for members with the Read-only role, in the SQL Editor and every read-only page.
readOnlyAccess.readOnlyQueriesSignInAs: Read-only queries sign in as {{user}}, which can read everything but cannot write, switch role or end other connections.
readOnlyAccess.theyRunInAReadOnly: They run in a read-only transaction, so data and schema can't change. Functions that act outside the transaction still work, for example ending other connections with pg_terminate_backend.
readOnlyAccess.readOnlyQueriesShareTheAdmin: Read-only queries share the admin database user
readOnlyAccess.createASeparateLoginOnThis: Create a separate login on this database (with pg_read_all_data) for read-only queries.
readOnlyAccess.thisDropsFromTheDatabaseRead: This drops {{user}} from the database. Read-only queries go back to running in a read-only transaction as the admin user.

rotateKeys.serversUsingTheCurrentSbSecret: Servers using the current sb_secret_ key stop working until they get the new one.
rotateKeys.appsUsingTheCurrentSbPublishable: Apps using the current sb_publishable_ key stop working until they get the new one.
rotateKeys.newSessionsAreSignedWithA: New sessions are signed with a new key. Sessions signed with the current one stay valid until the next rotation.
rotateKeys.theLegacyAnonAndServiceRole: The legacy anon and service_role keys are replaced; anything using them stops working.
rotateKeys.edgeFunctionsRestartWithTheNew: Edge Functions restart with the new password; nothing outside the stack uses it.
rotateKeys.s3ClientsUsingTheCurrentKeys: S3 clients using the current keys stop working; Storage restarts with new ones (Storage › S3 Connection).
rotateKeys.theStackIsBusyWaitFor: The stack is busy; wait for it to finish
rotateKeys.replaceKeysThatMayHaveLeaked: Replace keys that may have leaked. Supermixer writes the new values to the stack and restarts the services that use them.

rotationAdvice.lostAccessWhenTheProjectMoved: {{username}} lost access when the project moved to another organization {{when}}
rotationAdvice.theyCouldReadThisProjectS: They could read this project’s keys, or deploy Edge Functions that can, so they may still have them.
rotationAdvice.alsoCheckTheProjectForAnything: Also check the project for anything they may have left behind: Advisors › Changes compares the database with a snapshot from before.
rotationAdvice.rotateAtLeastTheSecretKey: Rotate at least the secret key, the legacy JWT secret and the Storage S3 access keys, together or one by one; this notice goes once all three are new.
rotationAdvice.rotateTheKeysWhereTheStack: Rotate the keys where the stack runs, update this project’s connection here, then dismiss this.

stack.supermixerIsStartingSupabaseSContainers: Supermixer is starting Supabase’s containers. The first stack can take several minutes while images download.
stack.itsContainersAreStoppedDataIs: Its containers are stopped; data is kept. Start it to use the project again.
stack.theLastOperationDidnTFinish: The last operation didn’t finish. Read the output below, then try again.
stack.supermixerIsWorkingOnTheStack: Supermixer is working on the stack.

upgrade.startTheStackToUpgradeIt: Start the stack to upgrade it
upgrade.theStackIsBusyWaitFor: The stack is busy; wait for it to finish
upgrade.theVersionOfSupabaseSSelf: The version of Supabase's self-hosting files this stack runs, and the one this Supermixer server bundles.
upgrade.newSettingsAddedToTheStack: New settings, added to the stack’s .env: {{join}}
upgrade.theDatabaseIsBackedUpFirst: The database is backed up first. Services whose image changes restart; the rest keep running.
upgrade.supermixerBacksTheDatabaseUpMoves: Supermixer backs the database up, moves the stack to supabase/docker @ {{short}}, pulls the new images and restarts the services that change, which are briefly unavailable. If the stack doesn’t come up, it goes back to its current version.

app.healthChecksRunWhileTheStack: Health checks run while the stack is running.

settingsApiKeys.keysYourAppsUseToCall: Keys your apps use to call this project's APIs. Public keys are safe in a browser when Row Level Security is enabled; secret keys bypass it.

settingsGeneral.whereSupermixerReachesThisStackLeave: Where Supermixer reaches this stack. Leave secret fields blank to keep their current values.
settingsGeneral.enterTheDatabasePasswordAndAn: Enter the database password and an admin key to test
settingsGeneral.moveThisProjectToAnotherOrganization: Move this project to another organization where you are an Owner. Project-scoped roles are removed.
settingsGeneral.onlyOwnersOfCanTransferIts: Only Owners of {{organizationName}} can transfer its projects.
settingsGeneral.youAreNotAnOwnerOf: You are not an Owner of any other organization.
settingsGeneral.supermixerCreatedThisStackSoDeleting: Supermixer created this stack, so deleting the project removes it: its containers, database, stored files and keys. This can’t be undone.
settingsGeneral.deleteThisProjectAndItsStack: Delete this project and its stack
settingsGeneral.supermixerForgetsThisProjectAndIts: Supermixer forgets this project and its stored credentials. The Supabase stack itself keeps running and is not changed.
settingsGeneral.itWillMoveToMembersOf: It will move to {{name}}. Members of {{organizationName}} lose access unless they also belong there.
settingsGeneral.itsContainersDatabaseStoredFilesAnd: Its containers, database, stored files and keys are deleted. This can’t be undone.
settingsGeneral.theSupabaseStackIsNotAffected: The Supabase stack is not affected. You can register it again later.

settingsInfrastructure.itsContainersPortsAndUpgradesAre: Its containers, ports and upgrades are managed where it runs. Projects created with “Create a new stack” are started, paused and restarted from here.
settingsInfrastructure.supermixerConnectsToThisStackIt: Supermixer connects to this stack; it didn't create it
settingsInfrastructure.supermixerCreatedThisStackAndRuns: Supermixer created this stack and runs it with Docker Compose on its server.
settingsInfrastructure.busyActionsReturnWhenItFinishes: Busy; actions return when it finishes.
settingsInfrastructure.asDockerComposeReportsThemRefreshed: As Docker Compose reports them, refreshed every 15 seconds.
settingsInfrastructure.theEndOfSupermixerSLog: The end of Supermixer’s log of docker compose commands for this stack.
settingsInfrastructure.itsContainersStopTheApiAnd: Its containers stop: the API and database go offline until you start it again. Data is kept.
settingsInfrastructure.everyServiceRestartsTheApiAnd: Every service restarts; the API and database are briefly unavailable.
settingsInfrastructure.supabaseCollectsThisProjectSLogs: Supabase collects this project's logs with Vector and keeps them with Logflare, for Logs Explorer, the API report and log drains. Together they use about 800 MB of memory.
settingsInfrastructure.turnThisProjectSLogsOn: turn this project's logs on or off
settingsInfrastructure.thisStopsLogflareAndVectorAnd: This stops Logflare and Vector and frees about 800 MB of memory. New logs won’t be saved, so Logs Explorer, the API report and log drains won’t work until you turn logs back on. Logs you already have are kept.
settingsInfrastructure.thisStartsLogflareAndVectorAgain: This starts Logflare and Vector again. They use about 800 MB of memory.
settingsInfrastructure.thisAppliesTheNextTimeYou: This applies the next time you start the stack.
settingsInfrastructure.whetherPeopleAndAppsReachThis: Whether people and apps reach this project's API over HTTPS and its database over an encrypted connection, using Supermixer's certificate.
settingsInfrastructure.supermixerDoesnTHaveACertificate: Supermixer doesn’t have a certificate yet. An instance admin sets one up in its settings first.
settingsInfrastructure.turnEncryptionOnOrOffFor: turn encryption on or off for this project
settingsInfrastructure.connectionsToThisProjectWonT: Connections to this project won’t be encrypted any more, and its URL becomes {{newURL}}.
settingsInfrastructure.itsUrlBecomesAndTheDatabase: Its URL becomes {{newURL}}, and the database only accepts encrypted connections.
settingsInfrastructure.databaseToolsNeedTheNewConnection: Database tools need the new connection string from Connect. People signed in to your apps may have to sign in again.
settingsInfrastructure.theApiAndDatabaseRestartBriefly: The API and database restart briefly.
settingsInfrastructure.supabaseStudioIsOffOnThis: Supabase Studio is off on this server. To run it in stacks Supermixer creates, set studio = true under [provisioning] and restart Supermixer.
settingsInfrastructure.supabaseStudioForThisStackAt: Supabase Studio for this stack, at its API URL. It asks for this login.
settingsInfrastructure.updateTheUrlInYourApps: Update the URL in your apps, and any sign-in callback URLs you’ve given GitHub, Google and the like.

settingsJwt.theSecretThatSignsThisStack: The secret that signs this stack's legacy API keys and user session tokens (JWT_SECRET).

settingsLogDrains.sendThisProjectSLogsTo: Send this project's logs to your own observability tools.
settingsLogDrains.itsLogsFlowWhereItRuns: Its logs flow where it runs: add a sink to its Vector configuration there. Projects created with “Create a new stack” get log drains here.
settingsLogDrains.supermixerConnectsToThisStackIt: Supermixer connects to this stack; it didn't create it

project.openTheOrganizationToSignIn: {{message}}. Open the organization to sign in with it.
